subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting for memory-pressure or event-loop-starvation cases remain an in-Gateway recovery path, or should OpenClaw add a supervisor/out-of-process started-without-success watchdog for macOS launchd cron runs?
rationale: Current code can mark interrupted runs after restart, but the issue discussion asks for alerting that survives a wedged Gateway process; that is a product and ownership choice rather than a narrow code repair.

options.title: Validate and design durable watchdog
options.body: Keep this issue open, run current-main macOS soak proof, and choose a durable cron lifecycle/failure-reporting model before assigning a fix.

options.title: Limit scope to memory retention
options.body: Treat failureAlert behavior as existing in-process semantics and only pursue a remaining memory/RSS leak if current-main soak reproduces it.

options.title: Close after fresh no-repro proof
options.body: Close only if a current-main launchd soak with comparable memory and cron load shows stable RSS/heap and visible cron failure outcomes.

recommendation.title: Validate and design durable watchdog
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, run current-main macOS soak proof, and choose a durable cron lifecycle/failure-reporting model before assigning a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The central suspected root remains memory-core watcher/search pressure, and lukeboyett authored the merged FD fan-out fix that any follow-up soak should validate first.
